title: Website Settings, Dev, Phone setup
body:
Add a Settings panel + a Claude dev panel + a "view as mobile" toggle

Assumes the site already exists. This adds a settings function, a lightweight "talk to Claude" panel, and a way to see the live site at phone width — nothing about building the site itself.

Add three draft-only features that sit outside the public navigation, in this order in the header (left to right): a mobile/desktop toggle, the gear, then the Claude icon.

- A Settings panel, opened by a small gear icon. Slides in from the right edge of the screen.
- A Claude panel, opened by a small Claude icon next to the gear. Also slides in from the right edge of the screen.
- A "view as mobile" toggle — a phone icon to the left of the gear. Clicking it narrows the page's own content wrapper to a chosen device's real logical width, so the live layout actually reflows (the same responsive rules that would apply at that width on a real phone fire for real) and the page stays fully interactive — this is a genuine resize of the real page, not a screenshot or a sandboxed iframe of it. Do this by giving the content wrapper `container-type: inline-size` and writing the site's responsive rules as `@container` queries scoped to it, rather than `@media` queries against the browser's own viewport — then the toggle can narrow that one element and have the real responsive behaviour follow, independent of how wide the browser window actually is. While active, the icon itself swaps to a desktop-monitor glyph; clicking it again restores the full-width desktop layout and swaps the icon back. Which device's width to use is itself a setting — a dropdown of a handful of current phones (e.g. a recent Samsung Galaxy, a recent iPhone, a smaller iPhone, a recent Pixel), each with its real viewport width/height, editable from the Settings panel's "Preview" group.

The Settings and Claude panels share the same edge and are mutually exclusive — opening one closes the other if it's open, so only one is ever showing at a time. The mobile toggle is independent of this — it's a standing layout state, not a transient panel, so it can be left on while either panel is opened or closed.

Neither side panel dims or blocks the rest of the page — the site stays fully interactive while one is open, so settings changes can be tuned live while watching the result underneath. Close a panel with its own × button, by clicking its icon again, or with Esc — not by clicking elsewhere on the page.

Both side panels carry a "Not part of the public site" label. Both show a version badge such as "Draft build v0.3 · 13 Nov 2026"; the same version also appears in the footer.

Theming foundation

Put every colour, font, size and spacing choice in CSS custom properties on :root. Do not hard-code them.
Use four font roles: --f-display (hero, big numbers, quotes), --f-head, --f-body and --f-ui (labels, nav, buttons). Add weight variables --w-display and --w-head.
Use scale multipliers that every size is multiplied by: --k-all, --k-body, --k-head, --k-display and --k-space. Also use --lh for line height and --wrap-w for content width. Write sizes as calc(clamp(...) * var(--k-head)).
Colour tokens switch through html[data-mode=dark] and html[data-accent=...] overrides.

Settings panel: "Global design controls"

Three groups of controls, each applied live — the panel sits over the page without blocking it, specifically so a change can be watched happening in real time:

Typography: four font dropdowns (display, heading, body, labels/nav/buttons), plus display and heading weight (Light, Regular, Medium). Offer around 15 fonts: this site's current brand font as the default, Century Gothic or system fonts, rounded and friendly options (Nunito, Quicksand, Varela Round, Fredoka, Figtree, Lexend), clean sans options (DM Sans, Outfit, Manrope, Poppins), serifs (Fraunces, Lora) and System default. Lazy-load Google Fonts only when a font is selected.
Size and spacing: sliders for overall text size, body, heading and display size, line spacing and section spacing, and a content-width selector (Narrow, Standard, Wide).
Look and feel: appearance (Light, Dark, Match this device), accent colour (the brand accent plus 3–4 alternatives), label style (UPPERCASE spaced or Sentence case), and animation (Full or Reduced).
Presets dropdown, with 5–6 named combinations (for example brand default, soft and friendly, classic serif headings, and a "large and clear" accessibility preset). Include a Reset to defaults button.
Copy settings button: writes a plain-text summary of every setting to a text box and to the clipboard, so it can be pasted back into a chat with Claude when a combination is chosen.
A type specimen panel showing display, heading, body and button text in the current settings.
A "Preview" group holding the mobile-device dropdown used by the header's view-as-mobile toggle.
Remember all settings in localStorage, wrapped in try/catch, and re-apply them on load. Dark mode must have a proper token set (check contrast, invert the logo, give light cards a dark equivalent). "Match this device" follows prefers-color-scheme. Reduced animation also respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Settings panel: other draft toggles

Add checkboxes for any draft-only aids on the site (for example "Highlight placeholders in red" and "Show hi-res photo reminder dots"), each remembered in localStorage and applied immediately — including to whatever's visible on the page behind the open panel.

Settings panel: Build

A short paragraph stating the current version, date and where earlier builds are archived.

Claude panel

A small "Claude" icon next to the gear opens a panel sliding in from the same edge as Settings (and mutually exclusive with it, as above), over the current page, without dimming or blocking it. It holds:

- Notes: a free-text box for typing review notes and change requests while looking at the current build. Saved into the repo (not just this browser's localStorage) — e.g. committed to a small notes file alongside the site — so the notes are still there next time, and so Claude can read them directly on request rather than relying on them being pasted back in.
- The current build version (same one shown in Settings and the footer).
- A list of previous builds, newest first, each linking to its archived copy.

The intended workflow: jot notes here while reviewing a build, then go back to Claude and ask it to read the notes and build the next version from them.

Versioning and Build History

Keep a small builds.json log (version, date, notes). Each new release gets a version number. Before overwriting the current site file, archive the previous version into a sibling Build History folder as index_v<version>_<date>.html. Rewrite the image paths in archived copies so they still work from that folder. Never silently overwrite a build.

Tip: replace the brand-specific bits (fonts, accent colours, draft toggles, the device list) with whatever fits the project at hand.

If you want the draft features removed at launch, add "provide a --public build that strips the Settings and Claude panels, the view-as-mobile toggle, their header icons, the draft toggles, and reverts the @container responsive rules back to plain @media" to the prompt.
